title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, Internal Tools (2026) - People Ops v2
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This consolidated handbook page provides practical, new-hire and manager-facing guidance for working at Redwood: company values and working norms, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding flow, and a concise internal tools reference. It is intended for new hires, hiring managers, and managers conducting career conversations. For discipline-level ladders and interview guides, follow the links in the Appendix.

---

1) Working at Redwood - values and operating norms

Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on production inference at scale. Our operating norms emphasize customer impact, measurable outcomes, and respectful collaboration. New hires should internalize these behaviors and model them in day-to-day work.

Key behaviors:
- Customer-first: prioritize reliability, security, and SLO-driven outcomes for customers.
- Ship early, iterate safely: prefer small, observable changes, feature flags, and gradual rollouts.
- Data-informed decisions: use metrics and postmortems to learn and improve.
- Respectful disagreement: document tradeoffs in ADRs and resolve by evidence.

Communication guidelines:
- Default to public channels: publish decisions and status in Confluence and team channels.
- Async-first: use written updates for cross-team communication; reserve meetings for complex alignment.
- Meeting hygiene: publish an agenda, outcome, and timebox for every meeting.

---

2) Roles & career ladders - summary and leveling guidance

Redwood maintains discipline-specific career ladders (Engineering, Product, Design, SRE, Data, People Ops, Sales). This summary is a quick reference; hiring and calibration use the full ladder rubrics.

Quick reference table:
- L1 (Associate / New grad): 0-2 yrs, IC. Learn the codebase, complete onboarding tasks, follow testing and runbook guidance.
- L2 (Software Engineer / Associate PM): 2-4 yrs, IC. Deliver features autonomously, own small services, add metrics.
- L3 (Senior / Lead IC or first-time manager): 4-7 yrs, IC/Manager. Drive cross-team work, mentor, design components for scale.
- L4 (Staff / Senior Manager): 7-12 yrs, IC/Manager. Lead architecture and mission outcomes, set roadmaps.
- L5 (Principal / Director): 12+ yrs, Leader. Define multi-quarter strategy, represent Redwood externally.

Leveling practices:
- Use the discipline ladder rubrics during hiring and promotion cycles.
- Promotion packets should include 3-5 impact examples, stakeholder feedback, and metrics.
- Calibration is evidence-based and facilitated by People Ops.

---

3) Benefits & perks (2026 highlights)

Redwood benefits support financial security, health, and work-life balance. Country-specific variants are available in the benefits appendix. Core offerings for full-time US employees:

Core benefits:
- Medical, dental, vision: multiple tiers with employer subsidy.
- Retirement: 401(k) with company match up to 4% after eligibility.
- Equity: new-hire grants plus refresh cycles managed by Compensation.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary caregiver, 6 weeks secondary caregiver, flexible phased return.
- Paid time off: 20 days PTO + 10 company holidays + 5 wellness days.

Perks and allowances:
- Home office stipend: $1,200 one-time + $60/month WFH allowance.
- Learning & development stipend: $2,000/year.
- Mental health & EAP coverage.
- Commuter benefits and relocation assistance (where applicable).
- Team budgets for quarterly offsites and hackdays.

Expense and reimbursement summary:
1. Submit expenses in Concur within 30 days.
2. Attach receipts and select policy tag (travel, learning, hardware).
3. Manager approves; Finance reviews for compliance.

---

4) Hiring & onboarding - flow and checklist

Objective: make hiring predictable and onboarding fast so new hires contribute within 30-60 days. This section covers the standard hiring flow, interview fairness rules, and a 30/60/90 onboarding template. Role-specific interview guides are linked in the Appendix.

Hiring flow (high level):
1. Requisition opened with role spec and timeline; People Ops posts to ATS.
2. Sourcing & initial screen by recruiting.
3. Interview loop (typically 4-6 interviews): technical/role fit, systems design, cross-functional, culture.
4. Debrief & calibration: panel submits feedback in ATS; hiring manager decides.
5. Offer creation, negotiation, and approval by People Ops.
6. Background checks and paperwork after verbal acceptance.

Interviewing and fairness rules:
- Standardized rubrics for all interviews.
- At least one interviewer trained in inclusive hiring per panel.
- Written feedback due within 48 hours.

Onboarding checklist (owner: Hiring Manager + Buddy + People Ops):
- Pre-boarding: equipment order, account provisioning, payroll paperwork, welcome packet.
- Day 0-1: Manager welcome, orientation (values, security basics), verify OKTA and email access.
- Week 1: Team introductions, first standup, required trainings (security, data handling).
- Days 15-30: First incremental deliverable, weekly 1:1s, mentor check-ins.
- 30/60/90 template:
  - 30 days: Learn codebase, ship a small fix or docs improvement, complete compliance trainings.
  - 60 days: Deliver a feature or measurable performance/regression fix.
  - 90 days: Own an end-to-end area and propose a 6-12 month improvement plan.

---

5) Internal tools quick reference

Primary tools and recommended starter actions (owners indicated):
- Slack (Eng Ops): Join #all, #announcements, and team channels; set status and notifications.
- Confluence (People Ops): Bookmark team pages; create a personal space for notes.
- GitHub (Eng Platform): Follow PR guidelines and branch naming; enable 2FA.
- CI/CD (CircleCI / Build System, Eng Infra): Read the CI runbook and monitor pipeline health.
- Datadog (Eng SRE): Access dashboards and configure SLO-aware alerts.
- PagerDuty (Eng SRE): Complete on-call training before rotation; review runbooks.
- Concur / Expensify (Finance): Submit expenses with correct policy tag.
- Okta (IT): Accept invite and enroll in MFA; request app access via Tools Access form.
- Internal Console & Prod Tools (Eng Platform / Eng SRE): Request access through manager approval; sign Prod Access Agreement.

Access process summary:
1. Okta invite from IT upon start.
2. Request additional apps via the Tools Access form in Confluence.
3. Manager approves role-specific production access.

---

6) Performance reviews, promotions & compensation cycle

Cadence and process:
- Company-wide review cadence: mid-year and year-end.
- Engineering uses ladder rubrics and calibration sessions.
- Promotion packet: candidate statement, manager assessment, peer feedback, and objective outcomes.
- Compensation changes are driven by the compensation committee recommendations; People Ops communicates timelines.

Manager responsibilities:
- Discuss career goals in 1:1s and document progression plans.
- Prepare promotion packets with evidence and stakeholder feedback.

---

7) Common forms, contacts, and escalation paths

Key contacts:
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai (hiring, benefits, payroll).
- IT Helpdesk: it-helpdesk@redwood.ai (hardware, Okta, app access).
- Security: security@redwood.ai (incidents, training questions).
- Finance: finance@redwood.ai (expenses, reimbursement policy).

Production incident escalation (customer-impacting outages):
1. Pager alert triggers on-call; on-call follows the incident runbook.
2. On-call pages team leads and Eng SRE.
3. If unresolved in 30 minutes, escalate to Engineering Director and head of SRE.
